title: Canonicalize ephemeral-prefix attribution for proxied/mirrored websocket sessions
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement:

We observe sporadic overcharging and attribution mismatches for streaming sessions when customer traffic passes through external reverse proxies or internal mirror/proxy layers (e.g., api-gateway -> sidecar-proxy -> multiplexer). Root causes identified in preliminary triage: ephemeral prefix replication (clients/edge proxies inject or strip short-lived prefixes/IDs), proxy-side buffering that splits frames mid-token, and mismatched provenance headers that cause the metering pipeline to treat identical fragments as distinct sessions. These manifest as: duplicated output token debits, orphaned input token credits, and customer support escalations.

Goal:
Canonicalize an "ephemeral-prefix attribution" translation layer near the edge of the metering pipeline so all proxied/mirrored websocket and HTTP-stream flows are normalized into a single provenance token. This ensures deterministic aggregation for token counts and aligns rate-limiter/quotas with expected session scopes.

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Design and implement a translation bridge in the session-ingress component that:
  - extracts provenance signals from known headers (x-rw-session, x-forwarded-for, x-rw-proxy-id) and websocket subprotocols,
  - normalizes ephemeral prefixes (strip/transform using canonical mapping rules),
  - emits a stable metering provenance id (mpid) for downstream ledger and rate-limiter components.
- Add heuristics to detect mid-token frame splits created by proxies and mark them for reassembly downstream before tokenization.
- Update metering ledger to accept mpid and use it for atomic credit/debit anchors.
- Add end-to-end tests and a reconciliation job to find historic mismatches caused by legacy behavior.

Out of scope for this ticket: altering customer-facing SDKs, wholesale rewrite of proxy stacks, or billing adjustments for historical charges (that will be handled via separate CS + billing efforts).
acceptance_criteria: Session ingress produces an mpid header on all proxied/mirrored websocket and HTTP-stream flows in staging
End-to-end test showing no duplicate token debits for a mirrored client -> proxy -> runtime path under simulated frame-splitting conditions
Metering ledger aggregates usage by mpid and produces identical totals to a non-proxied baseline for 99.99% of test permutations
Rate limiter uses mpid to apply quota semantics; unit tests verify quota consumption matches baseline scenarios
Reconciliation job identifies >95% of historic mismatches in a 7-day backfill sample and flags records for manual review
implementation_notes: Add a new component inside session-ingress: provenance-normalizer. It should be lightweight and implement a simple rule set (priority-ordered) for picking provenance signals.

Canonicalization rules (examples):
  - If x-rw-session present, use it after stripping ephemeral suffix (:<short-hash>)
  - If x-rw-proxy-id and x-forwarded-client both present, compose mpid = sha256(proxy-id + client-ip + first-8-chars-of-session)
  - If no known headers, fallback to connection-level GUID but mark as 'untrusted' for reconciliation

Implement a frame-inspection stage that detects token-boundary splits by checking for UTF-8 validity + known tokenizer delimiter heuristics. When suspected, tag the fragment 'reassembly_required' and route through the reassembler micro-path before tokenizer service.
Ledger changes: add 'mpid' column (string) to the session_anchors table and ensure indexes exist for queries by mpid + timestamp. Use upsert semantics to avoid duplication during racey writes.
Instrumentation: emit 'mpid_assigned' and 'mpid_conflict' traces. Add metric meters.metering.mpid_mappings.count and meters.metering.reassembly.detected.count with tag 'heuristic_reason'.
Backward compatibility: if downstream services don't understand mpid, session-ingress should still emit legacy headers (x-rw-original-session) for a 14-day rollout window.
test_plan: Unit tests for provenance-normalizer rule permutations (header-only, header+proxy, missing headers)
Property-based test that randomly injects ephemeral suffixes and verifies mpid stability for identical logical sessions
Integration test harness that replays previously captured proxy logs (s3://redwood-test-fixtures/proxy-frame-splits/), asserting ledger totals align with golden baseline
Chaos test: introduce small delays and duplicate frames from the proxy to ensure ledger dedupe logic holds
Reconciliation smoke: run reconciliation job on a 7-day window in staging and assert >95% of flagged records are explainable by known proxy patterns
rollout_plan: Feature branch -> internal code review -> QA in staging (use dedicated proxy topology) -> canary in production (5% of streaming traffic routed through new provenance-normalizer) -> monitor metrics and support tickets for 72hrs -> 30% canary -> full rollout
Enable 'strict_mpid' toggle in runtime so we can revert to legacy behavior quickly if regressions observed
Communicate to SRE and Billing: changes will add mpid column and new metrics. Coordinate DB migration during low-traffic window.
Post-rollout: run full reconciliation on first 72 hours of production traffic and compare to pre-rollout window for regression detection
